items.stem: A marketer needs to send to a frequently changing audience defined by purchase data. Which sending source is most appropriate?

options.rationale: A static list requires manual upkeep and suits stable audiences, not changing data-driven ones.

options.text: A data extension populated from purchase data
options.rationale: Correct: a data extension driven by purchase data handles dynamic, attribute-rich audiences.
Sending to All Subscribers ignores targeting and risks over-sending.
A test subscriber is for QA, not production sends.

items.explanation: Correct: a data extension driven by purchase data handles dynamic, attribute-rich audiences.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of a fallback (default) value in a personalization string?

options.rationale: Fallback values do not provide encryption.

options.text: To display substitute text when the attribute is missing
options.rationale: Correct: a default value renders substitute text so emails do not show blanks for missing data.
Fallback values have no effect on send throughput.
They have nothing to do with unsubscribe handling.

items.explanation: Correct: a default value renders substitute text so emails do not show blanks for missing data.

items.stem: Which TWO practices most directly support strong email deliverability?

options.rationale: Correct: domain authentication is a core deliverability practice.

options.text: Maintaining list hygiene by removing hard bounces
options.rationale: Correct: removing hard bounces protects sender reputation and deliverability.
Purchased lists harm reputation and deliverability and breach policy.

options.text: Embedding one large image as the whole email
options.rationale: Image-only emails trigger spam filters and hurt deliverability.

items.explanation: Correct: domain authentication is a core deliverability practice.
